title: A conditional abelianity theorem for special fourfold pairs with a half-weight divisor
main_claim: Assume the manifold abelianity theorem (every special compact Kähler manifold has a virtually abelian π1). Let X be a smooth projective fourfold and D a nonempty smooth connected divisor. If the root orbifold √[2](X,D) is special, then π1(X∖D)/⟨⟨γ²⟩⟩ is virtually abelian. The proof builds a smooth projective eightfold Y→X whose general fibre is a product of four elliptic curves, shows that Y is special, and shows that π1(Y) surjects onto the orbifold group.

issues.description: Specialness of the root orbifold is defined as having no orbifold line bundle L→Ω^p of Iitaka dimension p. The paper only sketches why this matches Campana's orbifold-special notion with fractional pole rules (Remark 2.3). The theorem is stated and proved with the paper's own definition, so this is not a gap in the proof. It only matters when connecting the result to Campana's conjecture.
issues.evidence: Remark rem:conventions compares the section lattices only in outline; the proof uses Definition def:special directly.

issues.description: The result is conditional on Theorem 1.1 of the companion paper (manifold abelianity in every dimension, used here in dimension 8). The paper states this condition openly. The sibling review of that companion paper (rank 60) found no gap.
issues.evidence: Theorem thm:main assumes Assumption ass:manifold explicitly.

coverage:
I read every section of the main paper (introduction, differentials, transfer, quadrics) and checked each step by hand. I skimmed only the list of files in the appendix (alternative branched construction) and did not audit it, and I did not audit the separate inertia document; neither is needed for the main proof. Steps checked:
(a) Lemma ratios (Bogomolov closed-form argument).
(b) The transfer criterion. On general fibres the filtration of Ω^p_Y|_F has trivial graded pieces, which gives a nowhere-vanishing section and so constant ratios. The ratios then descend by rational descent, and so do the tensor coefficients h_a. Pole testing via local sections of submersions over the general point of every base prime, including D in the root chart, is valid. The bound κ(K)≤κ(f*K)≤p holds.
(c) The π1 surjection: meridians of g*D have even multiplicity 2e and map to conjugates of γ^{2e}; surjectivity comes from Ehresmann with connected fibres.
(d) The construction. The quadrics are homogeneous: a_3∈M(−D) times v_3²∈T²=O(D) lands in M. The universal incidence is smooth and generic smoothness applies. Freeness: a fixed point over x∈D needs a degenerate column pair in each of the four matrices, so the bad locus has dimension ≤ dim A+3−4. A 2×3 submatrix of rank ≤1 has codimension 2, so Z has codimension ≥2 in X. A kernel vector with all entries nonzero gives a vertical Jacobian of rank 2 and hence submersive points, including at w=0. The complete intersection of two quadrics is a connected genus-one curve. S is finite over Q and therefore projective. There is a unique dominating component, and all the submersive points lie on it.
sibling_notes: This paper uses only Theorem 1.1 of the companion abelianity paper (rank 60, no_gap_found per the board), applied in dimension 8. The inertia/quotient-minimality alternative proof is a separate document and is not used here.
